notes: Condensed from the TokenMizer 0.4.2 storage-migration session. Long turns, mixed diagnosis and implementation, decisions justified by measurement.

messages.content: Do a deep audit of the persistence layer and fix what you find.
Found that graph_memory/persistence.py rewrites every node and edge as one JSON blob on every persist, once per chat turn. Cost is O(total graph) rather than O(changed).
that sounds bad for concurrency too
It is. Two processes holding one session each write the complete blob, so the later save discards everything the earlier one added. Decided: per-row storage, one row per node and per edge.
how will you know which rows changed?

Decided: derive the diff from state rather than tracking a dirty set. Node state is mutated from at least six places and a site that forgot to register would silently never reach disk. Implemented _serialize_state in persistence.py comparing each row against the exact string last written.
Completed: per-session migration in persistence.py that reads the v1 blob and writes it out as rows. The v1 row is kept, not deleted, so a downgrade still finds its data.
Created benchmarks/persistence/runner.py. Adding one node to a 151-node graph now writes 1 row instead of 151, and a turn that changes nothing writes 0 rows.
One: tests/unit/test_graph_persistence.py reached into the v1 graphs table directly. Fixed by porting it to the v2 schema. All 496 tests pass.
